title: Lock screen stays locked when a fingerprint or smartcard succeeds while the outputs are momentarily gone
line: A fingerprint or smartcard match now unlocks the screen even when it lands while the monitors are briefly gone on wake.
explanation: The unlock lived in the lock screen theme: LockScreenUi.qml handles onSucceeded and calls Qt.quit(), and the greeter only reacts to that. When a monitor wakes up the session can have no outputs for a moment, the greeter deletes every view and skips Qt's placeholder screen, so a fingerprint or smartcard success that lands in that gap reaches no QML and the session stays locked with the reader already spent. MR !352 (Rogerio Lucas) makes the greeter quit on PAM success itself, keeping the theme's confirmation only for a password stack that succeeds without prompting (no-password account), and also arms authentication from the greeter as soon as the lock is effective instead of waiting for the theme.

commits.message:
greeter: unlock from the greeter, not from the theme

A successful authentication only unlocked when the lock screen theme
called Qt.quit(), so a success arriving while no view existed, as when
the outputs vanish on wake, was lost. The greeter now quits by itself.

BUG: 523606

media.caption: Master, lock theme without an onSucceeded handler (the reporter's stand-in for 'no view'): the fingerprint matched 15 s ago and the screen is still locked.
MR !352, same theme and steps: the fingerprint match unlocks at once.

review.text: Unlocking from the greeter on PAM success, instead of waiting for the theme's Qt.quit(), fixes the real cause, and keeping the theme's confirmation only for a password stack that never prompted is right. This is the upstream MR !352 cherry-picked unchanged. Commit 1 has a real problem: armIfAuthenticating() runs on every readyChanged, but PamAuthenticator::cancel() also emits readyChanged (with m_ready=false) while PamAuthenticators' state is still Authenticating. So stopAuthenticating() calls tryUnlock() from inside cancel(), which starts a new worker for each authenticator it is stopping, and then sets the state to Idle with those workers running. The media only show the stand-in theme with no onSucceeded handler, not the real output-gap race, but the verification for that path is sound.
changes: In the readyChanged handlers (or in armIfAuthenticating), only re-arm when the authenticator became ready (isReady() true), so a cancel() inside stopAuthenticating() doesn't start new workers; raise this on MR !352.
Add a pamTest case: startAuthenticating() then stopAuthenticating() must leave no worker running and the state Idle.
